season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is fully cleared for camp off his Week 15 ACL/LCL tear and pushing for Week 1, with Eric Bieniemy back as OC and Kenneth Walker signed (3yr/$43M) to tilt KC run-heavy - protects Mahomes' knee and INT count while making Walker a goal-line RB2 with upside in this format.

Star RB hold-ins: Bijan Robinson (ATL) and Jahmyr Gibbs (DET) are both holding in over contracts - no lost value yet, but any escalation threatens early-season workloads for two elite non-PPR backs, so monitor daily.

The Raiders opened camp with Kirk Cousins named QB1 over No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza - stabilizes Brock Bowers (Cousins has force-fed TEs his whole career) and Ashton Jeanty volume, while Cousins' zero rushing caps his own value even at 6 points per passing TD.

WR musical chairs reshaped target maps: A.J. Brown traded to New England, Jaylen Waddle to Denver for a package including a 2026 first, Mike Evans signed with San Francisco, Michael Pittman dealt to Pittsburgh - each lands as a clear No. 1 or 1B, and the vacated targets lift Emeka Egbuka (TB) and Jayden Higgins (HOU).

Vikings QB battle between bargain signing Kyler Murray ($1.3M, with Arizona eating $35.8M) and J.J. McCarthy could run into September with local reports leaning Murray - a Murray win restores a discounted rushing-QB ceiling and stabilizes Justin Jefferson's downfield volume.

Atlanta acquired Tua Tagovailoa while Michael Penix Jr. rehabs his ACL and remains not cleared for 11-on-11 - Tua's quick accurate ball plus TE-friendly new HC Kevin Stefanski raises the floor for Drake London and newly extended Kyle Pitts.

Betting market: the Rams and Ravens top the board at 11.5 wins while Arizona sits alone at 3.5 - stack LAR/BAL TD equity, and treat Cardinals pass-catchers as garbage-time-only outside rookie RB Jeremiyah Love's volume.

New Orleans rebuilt around Tyler Shough, who closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus point fantasy games, adding Travis Etienne (4yr/$52M) and rookie WR Jordyn Tyson - a cheap ascending 6-pt-passing-TD stack while 31-year-old Alvin Kamara's role shrinks.

Coaching carousel is the biggest value-mover: Mike McDaniel now calls plays for the Chargers (Omarion Hampton), Todd Monken for the Browns, Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh, Brian Daboll in Tennessee, and John Harbaugh/Matt Nagy for the Giants - buy skill players whose new callers have a positional track record.

Week 1 injury-return watch: George Kittle (Achilles), Bo Nix (fractured ankle), Daniel Jones (Achilles), Rashee Rice (knee scope) and Malik Nabers (ACL, trending toward Week 1) all carry camp-setback risk that should discount them a round, not a tier.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett inherit a 3.5-win-total roster with Jacoby Brissett at QB after Kyler Murray's exit, so No. 3 overall pick RB Jeremiyah Love is the volume play and Marvin Harrison Jr. risks multi-TE formations capping his target share.

Kevin Stefanski (HC) and Tommy Rees (OC) bring a TE-friendly, run-committed scheme, but Bijan Robinson's hold-in and the Tua-over-rehabbing-Penix QB plan are the swing factors for Drake London and the newly extended Kyle Pitts.

First-year HC Jesse Minter with Payton-tree OC Declan Doyle keeps everything Lamar Jackson-centric - his rushing floor plus 6-pt passing TDs is a league-winner in this format, with Zay Flowers the downfield beneficiary and an 11.5 win total supporting the TD volume.

Joe Brady moves up to HC of a top-5 scoring offense and keeps his everybody-eats target spread - Josh Allen's rush-plus-passing-TD profile stays the No. 1 asset in this scoring, James Cook is the clear RB, and Dalton Kincaid stays capped.

Dave Canales returns a 7.5-win offense where a finally-healthy Jonathon Brooks (two ACLs, declared healthy) can eat into Chuba Hubbard's declining early-down efficiency - Brooks is the cheap side of that backfield.
The year-2 Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams offense vacated roughly 150 targets, setting up Luther Burden's big-play breakout, and a 9.5 win total backs the whole passing game's TD equity.

A 10.5 win total says the market trusts a stable Burrow-led high-TD passing attack that keeps his receivers premium at 6 points per passing TD, and the week's camp scare was defensive with Shemar Stewart carted off (verify).

Todd Monken's arrival plus an open Deshaun Watson vs Shedeur Sanders QB competition adds pass-game juice, and with David Njoku gone Harold Fannin is the featured TE while Quinshon Judkins (fibula) is expected for Week 1 (verify QB battle framing).
Quietest camp among the 9.5-win-total teams with no coaching or role shakeups surfacing this week, so price Cowboys skill players on continuity rather than change (verify).

Sean Payton stays heavily involved as Davis Webb takes OC, and the Jaylen Waddle trade gives Bo Nix (ankle, expected Week 1) a true separator - Waddle has a path to leading Denver in targets with Courtland Sutton as the aging TD complement.

Dan Campbell handed the offense to Drew Petzing and traded David Montgomery, so Jahmyr Gibbs - once his hold-in ends - inherits near-bell-cow work including goal line, top-3 non-PPR upside, while Petzing's history says temper Sam LaPorta.

Jordan Love's offense returns largely intact but Micah Parsons' torn ACL (targeting a postseason return) guts the defense, tilting Packers games toward shootouts that raise the passing game's TD ceiling.

An upgraded line and the David Montgomery trade give C.J. Stroud a real run game - Montgomery is a bell-cow goal-line value in non-PPR, with Nico Collins and riser Jayden Higgins soaking the downfield targets Christian Kirk left behind.

Daniel Jones (Achilles plus fibula) is expected for Week 1 but Michael Pittman was traded away, so this 7.5-win offense should funnel through the run game's volume and goal-line work rather than the thinned-out receiver room (verify backfield usage).

Liam Coen replaced Travis Etienne with a Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez committee (Coen has Kentucky history with Rodriguez), and fully-cleared Travis Hunter playing both ways adds a unique yardage-plus-big-play ceiling.

Eric Bieniemy back as OC plus Kenneth Walker signed points to a run-heavier under-center Chiefs look protecting Mahomes' surgically repaired knee - Walker's tackle-breaking and goal-line role plays up in non-PPR, and Rashee Rice (knee) is expected for Week 1.

Jim Harbaugh handing Mike McDaniel the playcalling is a real scheme jolt - outside zone and play action set up Omarion Hampton as a TD-leader RB1 bet, with Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey as efficiency winners.

The 11.5 win total is tied for the league's best and 38-year-old Matthew Stafford is coming off a 46-TD MVP season - the TD equity is real but you are paying peak price for the likeliest regression profile in football.

Klint Kubiak's run-first, two-wide, 12-personnel scheme with Kirk Cousins named QB1 over No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza concentrates the offense on Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty, though a 5.5 win total caps total TDs.

Full teardown - Waddle traded, Tyreek Hill released while injured, and new HC Jeff Hafley starting runner Malik Willis - leaves De'Von Achane (shoulder, expected Week 1) as the lone every-week piece and Willis as a dirt-cheap rushing-QB flier.

The Kyler Murray vs J.J. McCarthy battle may run to the season opener with local reports leaning Murray - Justin Jefferson's target dominance holds either way, and a Murray win adds a discounted rushing-QB ceiling play.

A 10.5 win total, a healthy-shouldered Drake Maye and the A.J. Brown trade make this an ascending 6-pt-passing-TD stack, with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson splitting the run game's value.

Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus point games and the Saints bought him Travis Etienne and rookie Jordyn Tyson - a cheap ascending passing game while 31-year-old Alvin Kamara's reception-based value plays down in non-PPR.

John Harbaugh (HC) and Matt Nagy (OC) inherit Jaxson Dart's near-Josh-Allen rushing production, Malik Nabers trending toward Week 1 off his ACL, and Isaiah Likely signed to be the featured mismatch TE - a sneaky TD-rich offense at a 7.5 win total.

Aaron Glenn's defense-first build with Frank Reich as OC leaves Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as talent plays trapped in an unsettled QB room at a 5.5 win total - yardage floors with thin TD ceilings.

With A.J. Brown traded and new OC Sean Mannion expected to stay run-heavy, Jalen Hurts' scoring already sagged without the tush push - his rushing keeps him a QB1 in this format, but the remaining pass-catchers are TD-dependent (verify Mannion tendencies).

Mike McCarthy takes over with Michael Pittman imported as the default No. 1 and Jaylen Warren positioned for a true three-down role after Kenny Gainwell's exit - the unsettled QB spot is the lid on the whole passing game (verify starter).

The champs lost playcaller Klint Kubiak and let Kenneth Walker walk while Zach Charbonnet works back from an ACL, making Jadarian Price the ascending back in a 10.5-win offense (verify new OC and Charbonnet timeline).

Kyle Shanahan (unhurt after a car wreck he admitted fault in) reloads with Mike Evans and his 11 straight 1,000-yard seasons while George Kittle pushes back from an Achilles - but Christian McCaffrey's 450-touch 2025 is the classic overwork red flag at his price.

New OC Zac Robinson inherits an offense without Mike Evans - Emeka Egbuka steps into the alpha red-zone role for aggressive Baker Mayfield, Bucky Irving (shoulder surgery, YPC collapse) now splits with Kenny Gainwell, and Vita Vea's trade-request hold-in is defense-side noise.

Robert Saleh (HC) and Brian Daboll (OC) rebuild around year-2 Cam Ward (8 TD to 1 INT over his final four games) with No. 4 pick Carnell Tate, $70M Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley - ascending, but 6.5-win volume and Wan'Dale's slot-compiler profile plays down in non-PPR.

Promoting David Blough to OC with zero play-calling experience is a red flag for a declining-efficiency Jayden Daniels - his legs keep the QB1 floor, Terry McLaurin anchors the outside, and new back Rachaad White's catch-first game loses value at zero PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's new Chargers scheme historically pumps RB efficiency (4.7 YPC for his backs) and Hampton posted an RB3-overall week before his 2025 ankle fracture - projected team TD leader, which is exactly what non-PPR pays for.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall pick with a three-down skill set and no real competition in Arizona; each of the last nine RBs drafted top-12 finished top-12 in fantasy, and raw volume plus goal-line work beats bad-team concerns in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's run-first two-wide scheme and a weak Raiders WR room funnel touches his way, and his 31.8-point Week 16 flashed the ceiling; improved infrastructure is the mechanism.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Travis Etienne's exit opens the Jacksonville lead role; a 31% missed-tackle-forced rate (second best) and 7 TDs on 93 rookie touches is an elite TD-per-touch profile for this scoring.

breakout_watch.name: David Montgomery
breakout_watch.why: Traded into a bell-cow void in Houston behind an upgraded line; his goal-line-heavy, zero-reception-dependent game is tailor-made for non-PPR at an RB23 price.

breakout_watch.name: Jonathon Brooks
breakout_watch.why: Declared healthy after two ACL tears with Dave Canales publicly backing him at an ADP near 125; Chuba Hubbard's grip on the Carolina backfield is weak and Brooks has the superior skill set.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Kenneth Walker left Seattle and Zach Charbonnet is coming off an ACL, leaving Price - 6.0 YPC and 13 TDs on limited college volume - the ascending back on a 10.5-win champion roster.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure hands him Tampa's alpha and red-zone role with aggressive Baker Mayfield; four 20-plus point games and 6 TDs as a rookie say the TD equity is already real.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Roughly 150 vacated Bears targets in year two of Ben Johnson's offense with Caleb Williams; rookie 2.92 yards per route run sat in the Chase/Jefferson tier, and his downfield YAC profile beats slot compiling in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Christian Kirk gone and Tank Dell still rehabbing in Houston; tied Nico Collins with 6 TDs as a rookie and produced when Collins missed time - TD-first WR at a discount.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six straight 17-plus point games to close 2025 plus a 22% share of Saints red-zone carries, now with Etienne and Jordyn Tyson added; 6-pt passing TDs and rushing yards at 10-per-point make him a top-12 QB bet at backup cost.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: His rookie rushing production trailed only Josh Allen per game, and new coordinator Matt Nagy plus Nabers' return add passing TDs on top of the rushing floor - premium profile in a 6-pt-pass-TD, rushing-friendly format.

breakout_watch.name: Malik Willis
breakout_watch.why: Averaged 23.3 fantasy points with about 60 rush yards and a rushing TD in his full-snap starts, and Miami's new regime signed him to start; at a QB21 price the rushing floor alone returns value in this scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Brock Bowers
breakout_watch.why: Kirk Cousins has force-fed tight ends his entire career (Reed, Rudolph, Hockenson) and Kubiak's 12-personnel base keeps Bowers on the field for a target monopoly - positional TD edge travels to any format.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age-38 encore to a 46-TD, 4,707-yard MVP season is the textbook TD-regression profile; even at 6 points per passing TD you are paying his ceiling as if it were the median outcome.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: A 450-touch 2025 puts him in the historical workload-cliff cohort at age 30; the first-round price ignores the bill coming due, and San Francisco added mouths around him.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Age 28 with 2,109 career touches, efficiency down to 4.0 YPC, a late-season injury fade, and reported off-field legal questions (verify status) - profile screams decline at a still-premium price.

fade_watch.name: Alvin Kamara
fade_watch.why: Age 31 off a career-low 657 scrimmage yards in 11 games while the Saints paid Travis Etienne $52M; his reception-based floor is worth zero in non-PPR.

fade_watch.name: Bucky Irving
fade_watch.why: Shoulder surgery, a YPC collapse from 5.4 to 3.4, a new playcaller with no loyalty to him, and Kenny Gainwell imported - the RB21 price assumes a bounce-back that camp has not yet confirmed.

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: Declining efficiency, minimal pass-game security, and a finally-healthy Jonathon Brooks behind him mean touch-share erosion risk every week.

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: Near-best-case rookie outcomes, David Njoku's exit inflating expectations, defenses now game-planning him, and limited offseason practice time - TD and efficiency regression baked into a premium TE price.

fade_watch.name: Sam LaPorta
fade_watch.why: New Lions OC Drew Petzing's Arizona offenses never featured elite TE usage and Detroit is expected to lean further into the run - top-TE price for TD-dependent usage.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Trending toward Week 1 off an ACL-plus-meniscus tear, but a cautious team and a run-first rookie QB cap early volume - elite talent, fade at last year's price and buy only at a discount.

uncertainty_note: Camp is only days old and several situations are genuinely live: the Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs hold-ins, the Vikings' Murray-McCarthy QB battle, the Vita Vea trade request, Pittsburgh's unsettled QB plan, Seattle's OC situation, and the Week 1 status of Mahomes, Kittle, Nabers, Bo Nix, Daniel Jones, Rashee Rice and Bucky Irving could all move sharply within days; additionally, a handful of player-team assignments and depth-chart details above come from fast-moving offseason reporting and are tagged (verify) where sourcing was thin.
